questions.def: Too means more than is necessary or desirable.
questions.question: The tea was ___ hot that I couldn't drink it.

questions.def: So modifies an adjective or adverb to show degree.
questions.question: She has ___ many books to read.

questions.def: 'Enough' goes after the adjective it modifies.
questions.question: He is ___ to reach the top shelf.

questions.def: 'Enough' means sufficient in quantity or degree.
questions.question: I don't have ___ money to buy that car.

questions.def: 'So' is used before an adjective to intensify it.
questions.question: The movie was ___ boring that I fell asleep.

questions.def: 'Too' goes before the adjective.
questions.question: The shoes were ___ for me to buy.

questions.def: Such is used with a/an + adjective + noun.
questions.question: She is ___ a good student!

questions.def: Too + adjective means more than is desirable.
questions.question: It's ___ cold to go swimming today.

questions.def: Too + adjective = more than desired.
questions.question: The shirt is ___ for me.

questions.def: So is used before an adjective to intensify it.
questions.question: He is ___ kind that everyone likes him.

questions.def: 'Enough' means sufficient quantity.
questions.question: I have ___ time to finish the project.

questions.def: 'So' is used to intensify an adjective.
questions.question: The music was ___ that I couldn't hear.

questions.def: Such + a/an + adjective + noun.
questions.question: It was ___ a difficult test that nobody passed.

questions.def: Too expresses excess or inability.
questions.question: I'm not ___ to go out tonight. I'm tired.

questions.def: 'Enough' goes after the adjective.
questions.question: I woke up ___ to catch the bus.

questions.def: Too indicates an excess of something.
questions.question: The coffee is ___ sweet for me.

questions.def: So is used to emphasize the quantity.
questions.question: She has ___ many clothes!

questions.def: Such + a/an + adjective + noun
questions.question: He is ___ a singer!

questions.def: Enough usually comes after the adjective.
questions.question: Are you ___ to start?

questions.def: Too + adjective means more than is manageable.
questions.question: The suitcase was ___ heavy to lift.

questions.def: 'Enough' follows the adjective to indicate sufficiency.
questions.question: She isn't ___ to lift that box.

questions.def: So much is used with uncountable nouns.
questions.question: There was ___ noise that I couldn't sleep.

questions.def: Enough means sufficient amount.
questions.question: He didn't study ___ to pass the exam.

questions.def: "Such" modifies a noun phrase (a good movie).
questions.question: It was ___ a good movie that I watched it twice.

questions.def: "Too" means more than is necessary or desirable.
questions.question: The coffee was ___ hot to drink immediately.

questions.def: "Enough" means sufficient, and comes before nouns.
questions.question: I don't have ___ money to buy a new car.

questions.def: "Too + adjective + to-infinitive" expresses an excessive degree: she is too tired to go out.
questions.question: She is ___ tired to go out tonight.

questions.def: With a noun, use "such" instead of "so".
questions.question: It was so beautiful day that we stayed outside.

questions.def: "So" modifies an adjective (interesting).
questions.question: The book was ___ that I couldn't put it down.

questions.def: "Such a" modifies a singular countable noun (noise).
questions.question: It was ___ that I couldn't sleep.
